entity.agency: Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC), Clerk's Office
entity.summary: Form a Virginia LLC by filing Articles of Organization with the State Corporation Commission, online or on paper.
entity.quote: File Online or complete Articles of Organization (Form LLC1011-DOC)

state_tax.summary: Register your business online with Virginia Tax to get account numbers for sales and use tax, withholding and other taxes.
state_tax.quote: When you complete your registration, you’ll receive your Virginia Tax account number for each tax type, your sales tax certificate (if you registered to collect retail sales or use tax)

unemployment.summary: You become liable for Virginia unemployment tax once you have a quarterly payroll of $1,500 or more or employ someone for 20 weeks in a year; register through VEC's iReg.
unemployment.quote: Have a quarterly payroll of $1,500 or more, or Employ someone for at least 20 weeks (about 4.5 months) in a calendar year

workers_comp.summary: A business with more than two employees regularly employed in Virginia must carry workers' comp. Contractors must count their subcontractors' employees toward that total.
workers_comp.quote: If the total of the contractor’s employees plus the sum total of subcontractors’ employees is more than two, then coverage is required.

local.summary: A state contractor license does not replace local licensing; check with your city or county Commissioner of the Revenue and Building Official.
local.quote: the business must also comply with local licensing requirements set forth by the localities (cities, towns, and counties) in which your business plans to do work

residential_building.name: Contractor License, Class A, B or C (Residential Building RBC or Home Improvement HIC classification)
residential_building.covers: Businesses doing construction, removal, repair or improvements over $1,000 per job; class depends on job size and yearly volume.
residential_building.threshold: Class C: jobs over $1,000 but less than $30,000; Class B: $30,000 to under $150,000; Class A: $150,000 or more.
prerequisites: Board-approved pre-license course completed by a member of responsible management or the designated employee
A Qualified Individual with 2 years (Class C), 3 years (Class B) or 5 years (Class A) of experience in the classification
Class A and B: a Designated Employee who has passed the business exams
Class A and B: minimum net worth ($15,000 for Class B, $45,000 for Class A) or a surety bond
residential_building.bond: Class A/B may use a surety bond to meet the financial requirement.
residential_building.summary: Virginia licenses contractor businesses in three classes based on job size. Even Class C (jobs over $1,000) requires a pre-license course and an experienced Qualified Individual; Classes A and B also need a Designated Employee who passed exams and a minimum net worth.
residential_building.quote: "Class C contractors" perform or manage construction, removal, repair, or improvements when (i) the total value referred to in a single contract or project is over $1,000 but less than $30,000

evidence.quote: the total value referred to in a single contract or project is $30,000 or more, but less than $150,000
"Class A contractors" perform or manage construction, removal, repair, or improvements when (i) the total value referred to in a single contract or project is $150,000 or more
Must have the minimum years of experience in the classification or specialty – 2 years for a Class C license, 3 years for a Class B license and 5 years for a Class A license.
All classes of license require the pre-license course to be completed.
worth/equity requirements (At least $15,000 for Class B or $45,000 for Class A applicants)
All Class A & Class B license applicants must declare a Designated Employee who has successfully completed the appropriate business examinations

commercial_building.name: Contractor License, Class A, B or C (Commercial Building CBC / Commercial Improvement CIC classification)
commercial_building.covers: Same class A/B/C license system as residential, with commercial classifications.
prerequisites: Pre-license course
Qualified Individual with required experience who passes the classification exam
Class A/B: Designated Employee exam and net worth
commercial_building.summary: Commercial contractors use the same DPOR Class A/B/C license, choosing the Commercial Building or Commercial Improvement classification. These designations require pre-approval and an exam.
commercial_building.quote: Applicants are required to be pre-approved and pass an examination for the following designations

evidence.quote: If you are applying for Commercial Building (CBC) or Commercial Improvement (CIC) only
All classes of license require the pre-license course to be completed.
"Class C contractors" perform or manage construction, removal, repair, or improvements when (i) the total value referred to in a single contract or project is over $1,000 but less than $30,000

electrical.name: Contractor License with Electrical (ELE) classification; Journeyman and Master Electrician tradesman licenses
electrical.agency: Virginia DPOR, Board for Contractors (Tradesman program)
electrical.covers: Electrical contractor businesses (need a master electrician) and individual electricians.
prerequisites: Journeyman: education plus practical experience (e.g., 240 hours of vocational training and four years of experience) and pass the exam
Master: hold a journeyman license for at least one year (or nine years of experience) and pass the exam
Contractor firm: a master tradesman license as a condition of licensure
electrical.summary: Virginia licenses electricians as journeymen and masters through DPOR, based on training, experience and an exam. An electrical contractor business needs a Class A/B/C contractor license, and the Board requires a master tradesman license for it.
electrical.quote: The Board shall require a master tradesmen license as a condition of licensure for electrical, plumbing, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning contractors.

evidence.quote: An applicant for examination to be licensed as a journeyman electrician, plumber, or HVAC tradesman must furnish evidence that one of the following experience and education standards has been attained
240 hours of formal vocational training in the trade Four years of practical experience in the trade for which licensure is desired
Having held a valid journeyman license in the trade for which licensure is desired for a minimum of one year
Nine years of practical experience in the trade for which licensure is desired.

plumbing.name: Contractor License with Plumbing (PLB) classification; Residential, Journeyman and Master Plumber tradesman licenses
plumbing.agency: Virginia DPOR, Board for Contractors (Tradesman program)
plumbing.covers: Plumbing contractor businesses (need a master plumber) and individual plumbers; a residential plumber license allows residential-only work.
prerequisites: Residential plumber: e.g., 160 hours of vocational training and two years of practical experience, plus exam
Journeyman: education plus practical experience, plus exam
Master: one year as a journeyman, three years as a residential tradesman, or nine years of experience, plus exam
Contractor firm: master tradesman license
plumbing.summary: Plumbers are licensed by DPOR as residential, journeyman or master tradesmen based on training, experience and an exam. A plumbing contractor business needs a contractor license backed by a master plumber.
plumbing.quote: The Board shall require a master tradesmen license as a condition of licensure for electrical, plumbing, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning contractors.

evidence.quote: 160 hours of formal vocational training in the trade Two years of practical experience in the trade for which licensure is desired
Having held a valid residential HVAC tradesman or residential plumber tradesman license in the trade for which licensure is desired for three years
Having held a valid journeyman license in the trade for which licensure is desired for a minimum of one year
Nine years of practical experience in the trade for which licensure is desired.

mechanical.name: Contractor License with HVAC (HVA) classification; Residential HVAC Mechanic, Journeyman and Master HVAC tradesman; Gas Fitter licenses
mechanical.agency: Virginia DPOR, Board for Contractors (Tradesman program)
mechanical.covers: HVAC contractor businesses and individual HVAC tradesmen; gas fitting, LP gas and natural gas fitting are separately licensed.
prerequisites: Residential HVAC or journeyman HVAC: vocational training plus practical experience, and pass the exam
Master HVAC: one year as a journeyman (or other listed path) and pass the exam
Contractor firm: master tradesman license
Gas fitter: training and experience per the gas fitter standards
mechanical.summary: Virginia licenses HVAC tradesmen (residential, journeyman, master) and gas fitters through DPOR. An HVAC contractor business needs a contractor license and a master HVAC tradesman.
mechanical.quote: The Board shall require a master tradesmen license as a condition of licensure for electrical, plumbing, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning contractors.

evidence.quote: An applicant for examination to be licensed as a residential HVAC tradesman or residential plumber tradesman must furnish evidence that one of the following experience and education standards has been attained
An applicant for examination to be licensed as a journeyman liquefied petroleum gas fitter, natural gas fitter provider, or gas fitter tradesman must furnish evidence

roofing.name: Contractor License, Class A, B or C with Roofing (ROC) specialty
prerequisites: Pre-license course
Qualified Individual with required experience, pre-approved and passing the roofing exam
roofing.summary: Roofing is a specialty classification on the Virginia contractor license. The Qualified Individual must be pre-approved and pass an exam for it.

evidence.quote: Applicants are required to be pre-approved and pass an examination for the following designations
"Class C contractors" perform or manage construction, removal, repair, or improvements when (i) the total value referred to in a single contract or project is over $1,000 but less than $30,000

pesticide.name: Pesticide Business License and Commercial Pesticide Applicator certification
pesticide.agency: Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (VDACS), Office of Pesticide Services
pesticide.covers: Any business that applies, sells, mixes or recommends pesticides for pay, and the applicators who apply them.
prerequisites: Pass the Commercial Pesticide Applicator Examination (applicators)
Business license applicant or an employee passes a written exam (waived if a certified commercial applicator)
pesticide.summary: Businesses applying pesticides for pay need a VDACS Pesticide Business License, and applicators must pass the commercial applicator exam to be certified.
pesticide.quote: A pesticide business license is required for any person or business operating in Virginia, which, in

evidence.quote: applicant or his employee is certified as a commercial applicator, the exam requirement is waived.
Apply to the Office of Pesticide Services to take the Commercial Pesticide Applicator Examination.

asbestos.name: Asbestos Contractor License (and individual asbestos worker/supervisor licenses)
asbestos.agency: Virginia DPOR, Board for Asbestos, Lead, and Home Inspectors
asbestos.covers: Anyone contracting for pay to carry out or work on an asbestos project.
prerequisites: DPOR asbestos contractor license; workers and supervisors individually licensed after accredited training
asbestos.summary: It is illegal to contract for asbestos work in Virginia without a DPOR asbestos contractor license; individual asbestos workers and supervisors are licensed by the same board.
asbestos.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person who does not have an asbestos contractor's license to contract with another person, for compensation, to carry out an asbestos project or to perform any work on an asbestos project.

evidence.quote: The Board for Asbestos, Lead, and Home Inspectors licenses individuals engaged in asbestos remediation, lead-based paint remediation and renovation, and home inspection.

lead_rrp.name: EPA RRP Firm Certification and Certified Renovator (federal)
lead_rrp.covers: Firms doing renovation, repair or painting that disturbs paint in pre-1978 homes and child-occupied facilities.
prerequisites: EPA RRP firm certification
Certified renovator training
lead_rrp.summary: Virginia is not an EPA-authorized RRP state, so renovation firms get RRP certification directly from EPA. Lead abatement (not routine renovation) is licensed separately by DPOR.
lead_rrp.quote: EPA's renovation program applies to all states, Tribes and territories where EPA has not specifically provided authorization for that state, Tribe or territory to operate the program themselves.
lead_rrp.note: Virginia is not in EPA's list of authorized RRP states on this page.

evidence.quote: Federal law requires all renovation, repair, and painting firms (including sole proprietorships) working in housing, or facilities where children are routinely present, built before 1978, to be certified.

other.name: Gas Fitter, LP Gas Fitter, Natural Gas Fitter Provider licenses
other.summary: Gas fitting work requires a DPOR gas fitter license based on training and experience.
other.quote: An applicant for examination to be licensed as a journeyman liquefied petroleum gas fitter, natural gas fitter provider, or gas fitter tradesman must furnish evidence

other.summary: Landscape irrigation and landscape services are contractor classifications requiring pre-approval and an exam.
other.quote: CIC – Commercial improvement ISC – Landscape irrigation
